item.description:

The ultimate objective of the REACT-FIBER project is to develop, validate and demonstrate at pilot scale an integrated, industrially scalable technological supply chain for the high-value recycling of Carbon Fiber Sheet Molding Compound (CF-SMC) materials. The activities planned under this assignment relate to OR2: Analysis of the quality of carbon fibers recycled from SMC, with particular reference to: • A2.1 – Optimization of carbon fiber recycling from cured SMC • A2.2 – Assessment of the feasibility of extending the recycling process to uncured scrap

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Sviluppo e studio meccanicistico di metodologie catalitiche stereoselettive per trasformazioni radicaliche (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-04 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-05 Chimica organica

The research will focus on developing new stereoselective methodologies for radical transformations, combining synthetic organic chemistry, transition-metal catalysis and visible-light photochemistry. Activities will include the design and optimization of catalytic reactions, investigation of substrate scope, synthesis and characterization of organic compounds, and mechanistic studies aimed at understanding radical reactivity and stereocontrol. The resulting catalytic concepts will contribute to the development of innovative catalytic systems within the ERC PHOTOZYME project, including their potential application to light-driven enzymatic transformations.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Identification of emerging allergens in the durum wheat supply chain (Univ. PARMA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-04 23:59
Institution: Univ. PARMA, Parma
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-05 Chimica organica

The focus of this project is the study of certain allergens (mustard, lupine, soy) selected because they have a non-negligible probability of being present in the durum wheat supply chain following field contamination, in relation to farming practices and climatic conditions. Special emphasis will be placed on the development and subsequent application of innovative methods based on the LC-MS technique, capable of overcoming the limitations of the other techniques commonly used.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development, optimization and application of conventional and green analytical methods based on liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry ("Campus Bio-Medico")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-03 12:00
Institution: "Campus Bio-Medico", Rome
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-01 Chimica analitica, ambientale e dei beni culturali

The overall objective of the project is to develop, optimize and validate innovative analytical methods combining conventional and green sample preparation techniques with high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry analysis. These methods will be applied for the determination of different classes of molecules in biological samples of clinical and nutritional interest, as well as in food matrices, including endogenous bioactive compounds present in foods and agri-food industry by-products, and exogenous molecules.

the proposed research programme pursues two complementary objectives. First, it aims to develop an integrated analytical platform capable of comprehensively assessing both the safety and nutritional quality of innovative protein ingredients through the application of state-of-the-art analytical methodologies. Second, it seeks to implement a range of capacity-building and knowledge-transfer activities for researchers from the MENA region through blended learning, online education, and on-site training programmes, thereby strengthening scientific expertise and fostering long-term international collaboration

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Novel Photocatalytic Strategies for Organoboron Chemistry - 2026_IDR_DCMC_22 (Politecnico MILANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

The project aims to develop innovative photocatalytic strategies for the sustainable synthesis of organoboron compounds (OBCs), fundamental in organic chemistry and crucial for the pharmaceutical and materials sectors. Since traditional methods based on carbanion chemistry are poorly sustainable, an efficient and eco-compatible approach driven by visible light is proposed. Photocatalysis grants access to open-shell intermediates under mild conditions, a reactivity suited to boron substrates, whose vacant p orbital favours radical stabilisation. Recovery and/or upcycling of organic material from rechargeable battery electrodes using non‑conventional sustainable solvents aims to establish low‑impact processes for selectively extracting, purifying, and revalorizing polymeric binders, conductive additives, and organic degradation products from spent electrodes.
